high.title: Fed Chair Considers Major Changes, Markets Get Even Fewer Clues on Interest Rates
high.summary: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh is reportedly considering reducing the number of FOMC meetings per year — currently set at 8 — which would represent a significant structural shift in U.S. monetary policy communication. At the July 30th FOMC meeting, policymakers voted 9-3 to hold rates steady, a decision largely anticipated by markets. However, investor reaction turned negative as Warsh declined to elaborate on the rationale for the hold or signal whether he would support rate hikes if inflation fails to continue declining. Since assuming the chairmanship in May, Warsh has signaled a more opaque communication style, leaving markets with fewer forward-guidance anchors.

high.title: Why it matters for VND/USD and Vietnamese assets:
SBV Raises State Treasury Deposit Inclusion Rate in LDR Calculation to 50%, Effective August 1st
high.summary: On July 30, 2026, the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) issued Decision No. 1743/QĐ-NHNN, raising the deduction ratio for State Treasury term deposits when calculating the Loan-to-Deposit Ratio (LDR) to **50%**, effective August 1, 2026 through July 31, 2028. This is a meaningful regulatory easing: by allowing banks to exclude 50% of State Treasury deposits from their LDR denominator, the SBV is effectively loosening the LDR constraint for commercial banks that hold these deposits, freeing up lending capacity without requiring additional retail deposit mobilization.

high.title: Bank Deposit Interest Rates on August 2 at Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank, MB, Sacombank, HDBank...
high.summary:
As Vietnam enters August 2026, deposit interest rates across the banking system remain broadly stable, with no significant new adjustments recorded. A survey of 34 banks shows 12-month deposit rates ranging from **3.7% to 7.8% per annum** — a wide spread of 410 basis points between the highest and lowest-offering institutions. **ACB leads the market** at 7.8%/year for 12-month tenors, also offering 7.6% (6-month) and 7.7% (9-month). Saigonbank ranks second at 7.2%, followed by Bac A Bank at 7.1%. Seven banks in total now offer ≥7%/year on 12-month deposits, including MBV, VCBNeo, PGBank, and VIB. Competition for deposits remains concentrated among small-to-mid-sized banks. **For bond and FX traders**, the persistence of elevated deposit rates — particularly at smaller banks — signals continued liquidity competition in the system. The wide rate differential versus state-owned banks (Agribank, BIDV, Vietcombank, VietinBank) suggests bifurcated funding conditions. Sustained high deposit rates could compress bank NIMs and may limit further monetary easing, a key watch point for government bond yield direction.

medium.title: Vietnamese Stock Market Weekly Recap: TAL and FRT Shares Surge to Upper Circuit, PNJ Hits 6-Year Low
medium.summary:
The VN-Index closed the final session of the week (July 31st) on a volatile note — opening with a gain of over 13 points before a sharp afternoon sell-off erased all gains, with the index ultimately falling nearly 9 points as selling pressure overwhelmed buyers. TAL (Taseco Real Estate Investment JSC) and FRT were the standout performers, both hitting their daily upper-circuit limits with no sellers remaining. TAL surged 6.97% to VND 22,250/share, driven by a blockbuster Q2/2026 result showing after-tax profit of VND 158 billion, up over 320% year-on-year. Meanwhile, PNJ (Phu Nhuan Jewelry) continued its underperformance, touching a 6-year price low. The broader market's inability to hold morning gains despite positive catalysts suggests underlying caution among investors, which is consistent with a risk-off tone potentially driven by external headwinds including USD strength and Fed uncertainty. **Relevance:** VN-Index sentiment and liquidity are key indicators for foreign equity flow tracking.

medium.title: New Rankings: Top 10 Most Profitable Banks in Vietnam — H1 2026 Update
medium.summary: Vietnam's banking sector delivered robust H1 2026 earnings, with aggregate pre-tax profit across 28 banks reaching approximately VND 223.7 trillion (~USD 8.7bn), up ~21% year-on-year from VND 184.8 trillion in H1 2025. The top 10 banks — Vietcombank, VietinBank, MB, BIDV, VPBank, Techcombank, Agribank, HDBank, ACB, and SHB — collectively earned VND 183.1 trillion, up 29.1% YoY, now representing ~82% of sector-wide profits (vs. ~77% in H1 2025), signaling accelerating profit concentration among large state-linked and systemically important banks. Smaller and mid-tier banks lagged significantly, with some seeing profits fall more than 70% YoY. For bond and equity investors, the strong earnings profile of top-tier banks supports capital adequacy buffers and reduces near-term credit risk concerns, which is constructive for Vietnamese bank bonds and their equity valuations. However, the divergence between large and small banks warrants monitoring for systemic stress at the tail end of the sector, which could have implications for SBV's policy stance on credit conditions.

medium.title: Full Banking Sector Profit Overview — 27 Banks in H1 2026: Vietcombank, VietinBank, MB, SHB, Sacombank and Others
medium.summary: Detailed H1 2026 results confirm strong momentum at the top of the sector. Vietcombank — the bellwether state bank closely watched for FX and monetary policy signals — posted Q2 2026 pre-tax profit of VND 17.42 trillion, surging 57.9% YoY, with H1 total assets rising 8.8% YTD to VND 2.657 quadrillion. Customer loans grew 5.1% and deposits 3.4% vs. end-2025. MB posted Q2 pre-tax profit of VND 10.56 trillion (+40.7% YoY), with H1 cumulative profit of VND 20.19 trillion (+27.1%), placing it in the top 3 system-wide. Net interest income growth of 35%+ at both institutions suggests healthy NIM expansion, likely supported by the current interest rate environment. For VND bond traders, Vietcombank's balance sheet expansion and strong deposit franchise reinforce its role as a key liquidity anchor in the domestic interbank and government bond markets. Watch for any guidance on loan growth targets for H2 2026 which could signal SBV credit quota (room) allocations.

medium.title: Vietcombank, VietinBank, Agribank and Others to Suspend All Withdrawal/Transfer Transactions for Non-Compliant Accounts
medium.summary: Major Vietnamese banks including Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank, Agribank, MB, and VPBank are implementing new SBV regulations under Circulars 17/2024/TT-NHNN and 18/2024/TT-NHNN, which mandate full identity document verification and biometric authentication for all account holders. Accounts that have not completed the update process will face full suspension of transactions — including counter withdrawals, online transfers, bill payments, and ATM/POS transactions. The policy's stated goal is to strengthen payment security and enforce "true owner" authentication. While primarily a consumer banking/compliance story, this regulation is relevant to the broader banking sector outlook as it could temporarily disrupt payment volumes and liquidity flows at the retail level. Mass account freezes at systemically important banks could create short-term friction in domestic payment settlement. International fund managers should note this reflects the SBV's continued push toward a more regulated, digitally verified banking infrastructure — a medium-term positive for sector governance and AML compliance standards.

medium.title: Bank Deposit Interest Rates as of July 30th: Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank, MB, Sacombank, HDBank...
medium.summary: Deposit rates across Vietnamese banks remained broadly stable as of July 30, 2026, with no new material adjustments recorded. ACB leads the market at **7.8%/year** for 12-month terms, followed by Saigonbank (7.2%) and Bac A Bank (7.1%). A total of 7 banks now offer 7% or above for 12-month deposits. The Big 4 state-owned banks (Agribank, BIDV, Vietcombank, VietinBank) uniformly maintain **6.8%/year** for 12- and 18-month terms. The stabilization in deposit rates following earlier localized adjustments suggests the market is in a consolidation phase, with no imminent upward rate pressure — a relatively benign signal for VND bond yields in the near term.

medium.title: Bank Deposit Interest Rates as of July 31st: Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank, MB, Sacombank, HDBank...
medium.summary: Entering the final day of July 2026, the deposit rate landscape remained virtually unchanged, confirming the market's current stable footing. ACB retains the top spot at **7.8%/year** (12-month), with the Big 4 holding steady at **6.8%/year**. The rate structure — with higher rates concentrated among small-to-mid sized banks — continues to reflect a two-tier market dynamic. For bond traders, the absence of upward deposit rate pressure into month-end is constructive for government bond valuations, as it reduces the risk of deposits competing aggressively with fixed-income instruments for investor flows.

medium.title: Vietnamese Equities: After the Steepest Drop of the Year — Will August Breathe Easier?
medium.summary: The VN-Index closed July on a positive note, reversing course to end the final week up 2.95% at 1,735 points — recovering the key 1,700 level after what the article describes as the sharpest single-period decline of 2026. The rebound was broad-based, with gains across banking, technology, steel, retail, real estate, insurance, energy, and fertilizer sectors. The primary catalyst was the peak of Q2 earnings season, with large-cap companies reporting strong profit growth that drew money back into the market. However, liquidity declined approximately 10.3% week-on-week, signaling that the recovery remains selective rather than broad-based, with flows concentrating in fundamentally sound names. For fund managers, the equity recovery is relevant as a risk-sentiment indicator for broader Vietnamese asset classes. A sustained VN-Index recovery above 1,735 could support foreign portfolio inflows, which would provide mild VND tailwinds. The liquidity contraction warrants caution — watch Q2 earnings momentum and whether foreign net buying resumes in August.

medium.title: VinaCapital Expert: History Shows Vietnamese Equities Can Recover 80–100% After Sharp Drops
medium.summary: VinaCapital's Senior Investment Director, Dinh Duc Minh, speaking at Fmarket's FunInsider forum on the theme "Are Market Valuations Entering an Attractive Zone?", argued that every major Vietnamese market correction — including the COVID-19 crash, the Van Thinh Phat/corporate bond crisis, and the recent US tariff shock on Vietnamese goods — has pushed valuations into deeply cheap territory, historically followed by 1–2 year recovery cycles with total gains of 80–100% from trough. This commentary is relevant for international fund managers considering re-entry timing into Vietnamese equities. The explicit reference to US import tariffs as the most recent shock is a reminder that trade policy remains a key macro risk for VND and Vietnamese risk assets. A sustained re-rating of Vietnamese equities would attract foreign portfolio inflows, supporting the VND and reducing pressure on SBV FX intervention. Monitor foreign net buying data and P/E valuation levels as leading signals.

medium.title: Bank Deposit Interest Rates on August 1 at Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank, MB, Sacombank, HDBank...
medium.summary: This article provides the August 1 deposit rate snapshot, confirming rate stability heading into the new month following isolated adjustments in July. ACB again leads at 7.8%/year for 12-month deposits, with the four major state-owned banks (Agribank, BIDV, Vietcombank, VietinBank) uniformly holding at **6.8%/year** for 12-month tenors. LPBank, BVBank, and OCB form a secondary tier at 6.9%/year. The consistency between the August 1 and August 2 snapshots confirms there is no new easing or tightening impulse from the banking sector at the start of Q3 2026. For government bond investors, the state-bank deposit rate floor of 6.8% provides a useful benchmark for short-to-medium duration bond pricing; any compression in this rate would be a bullish signal for VGB yields.

medium.title: Gold Ring and Gold Bar Prices Today, August 2
medium.summary: Domestic gold prices in Vietnam remain elevated, with SJC gold bars quoted at **VND 137–141 million/tael** (buy/sell) and plain gold rings at **VND 136–142 million/tael**. Prices peaked during the week on July 28 before retreating. International spot gold closed the week at **USD 4,041/ounce**, supported by dip-buying and cooling inflation data. While gold is not a direct VND/USD instrument, domestic gold price dynamics in Vietnam are closely watched as a proxy for USD demand and capital flight risk — elevated gold prices and strong domestic demand can pressure FX reserves and the VND. The reference to cooling global inflation is also relevant for USD outlook and, by extension, SBV's FX management stance.
